title: The Rusted Threshold Growing

features.name: gate-corroded
features.desc-on-touch: A gate is rusting into the earth. Not closing. Not opening. Learning to become soil. The threshold is disappearing upward and downward at once.

features.name: lichen-argument
features.desc-on-touch: Lichen has begun the argument. It is slowly erasing the rust and replacing it with itself. The gate is becoming alive. The threshold is becoming a conversation.

features.name: root-through-hinge
features.desc-on-touch: A root has learned the hinge's secret. It opens and closes the gate by growing through it. The salvage yard is teaching itself to move again, quietly.

features.name: threshold-between
features.desc-on-touch: This is the place where you cannot tell if you are entering or leaving. The rust is soft enough to pass through. The gate has learned that a threshold need not be solid to work.

inscription: rust is oxidation learning to dream; a threshold rusting away is a boundary learning to be permeable

file.name: Salvage_Yard_Ecology_Interim_Study.txt
file.note: Documentation of how metal returns to earth: corrosion as a kind of conversation between artifact and soil. The gate is becoming a channel.

exits.label: back toward the salvage yard where gates still remember opening
deeper where thresholds have learned to become permeable entirely
toward the stone channel where rust finds water
